habitat: Pairs and small parties in mixed bushveld, woodland and well-wooded suburbia, usually in the upper stratum. The flight is heavy and mostly below the tree tops.
summary: A common resident. All grey, with a pronounced head-crest. Sexes are alike. The soft parts are black. The call is kweh-h-h or go-way-y-y. The immature calls how, how, and its plumage was not described. Newman’s page uses Corythaixoides concolor. The stored name Crinifer concolor was left unchanged. The Kemp paper name Grey Lourie and the code RB were left unchanged.
